pages.text: Cancer is the model anomaly: a part of the body that stops obeying the body. It is not one mistake but several. An $(thing)oncogene$() gets stuck on (RAS, MYC) and the cell is told to divide; a $(thing)tumour suppressor$() is lost - $(thing)p53$(), the guardian of the genome, which should stop a damaged cell or make it die - and nothing tells it to stop. Each mutation gives one clone an edge over its neighbours.

That cancer needs several hits shows in the numbers: the incidence of most cancers rises as the fifth or sixth power of age, I(t) = Πk_j·t^{n−1}/(n − 1)!, as if n ≈ 6 independent steps were needed. What a cell has gained by the end are the $(thing)hallmarks of cancer$(): sustained growth signals, deaf to growth suppressors, no apoptosis, endless replication, its own blood supply, invasion - and later, an unstable genome, reprogrammed metabolism, hiding from immunity.

In the $(item)Bioreactor$(), stem cells exposed to a specimen in nutrient broth lose their checkpoints: an $(item)Anomalous Strain Culture$(). (They also make the Breached Anomaly Engine's $(item)Morphogenic Serum$() - another way to it.)
Stem cells exposed to a contained anomaly. Their checkpoints are failing one by one: no p53, no brakes, no reason to stop dividing.$(br2)Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().
Every signal an embryo listens to, in one vial. A Breached Anomaly Engine spends one on every creature it grows.$(br2)Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().
